subject: Full Test
topic: Full syllabus — all subjects A-E (exam simulation)

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Which article correctly fills the gap: The colonel described it as ______ one-sided contest from the very start.
questions.explanation: The word 'one' begins with the consonant sound /w/ even though its first letter is a vowel, so it takes 'a' — 'a one-sided contest', 'a one-rupee coin'. 'an' is wrong because 'an' is used only before an initial VOWEL SOUND, and 'one' does not have one. 'the' is wrong because the contest is being described as one of a class for the first time, not identified as already known to the listener. 'no article' is wrong because 'contest' is a singular countable noun and cannot stand bare in this position.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Quit India Resolution was passed by the All India Congress Committee at Bombay on which date?
questions.explanation: The AICC session at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay adopted the Quit India Resolution on 8 August 1942, after which Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call. 9 August 1942 is wrong because that is the date the mass movement actually began following the pre-dawn arrest of the leaders, not the date the resolution was passed. 14 July 1942 is wrong because that is when the Congress Working Committee at Wardha approved the draft resolution which was later placed before the AICC. 26 January 1942 is wrong because 26 January relates to the Independence Day pledge of 1930 and later to Republic Day, not to Quit India.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The price of a commodity is first increased by 25% and then the increased price is decreased by 20%. The net effect on the original price is:
questions.explanation: Take the original price as 100. After a 25% increase it becomes 125. A 20% decrease of 125 is 25, so the price returns to 100 — a net change of zero. '5% increase' is wrong because it comes from simply subtracting 20 from 25, which ignores that the second percentage acts on the larger amount 125, not on 100. '5% decrease' is wrong for the same reason with the sign reversed. '1% decrease' is wrong because it wrongly applies the successive-change formula as (+25) + (-20) + (25 x -20)/100 with a mis-signed product; the correct successive formula gives 25 - 20 - 5 = 0.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a pointing device that works through a pressure-sensitive surface and is normally built into laptop computers?
questions.explanation: A touchpad (trackpad) is a flat, pressure- and motion-sensitive surface integrated into laptops; finger movement on it moves the on-screen pointer. 'Trackball' is wrong because it is a ball rotated in a socket, usually an external unit, and is not a pressure-sensitive flat surface. 'Joystick' is wrong because it is a lever-based device used mainly for gaming and simulation, not a laptop's built-in pointer. 'Light pen' is wrong because it is a pen-like device that detects light directly from a monitor's surface and must be pointed at a screen, not built into the palm rest of a laptop.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Sindh nallah, the largest tributary of the Jhelum within the Kashmir valley, joins the Jhelum near which place?
questions.explanation: The Sindh nallah rises in the Machoi glacier area, flows through Ganderbal district and meets the Jhelum at Shadipur, a confluence locally revered as Prayag. 'Khanabal' is wrong because Khanabal near Anantnag is a point on the upper Jhelum where the Arapath and other feeders join, not the Sindh. 'Verinag' is wrong because Verinag is the traditional SOURCE spring of the Jhelum itself. 'Baramulla' is wrong because Baramulla lies far downstream, beyond the Wular lake, where the Jhelum leaves the valley through a gorge.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: The witness was accused __________ concealing material facts from the investigating officer. Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: __________
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'accuse somebody OF something', so 'accused of concealing' is correct. 'for' is wrong because 'for' follows verbs such as blame, punish and criticise ('blamed for concealing'), not accuse. 'with' is wrong because 'with' follows 'charge' ('charged with concealing'), a related but distinct legal verb. 'about' is wrong because 'about' introduces a topic after verbs like speak, inform or complain, and cannot express the offence attributed to a person after 'accuse'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the personalities in Column I with their popular names in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Lal Bahadur Shastri
(b) Chittaranjan Das
(c) Madan Mohan Malaviya
(d) Bal Gangadhar Tilak

Column II:
(i) Lokmanya
(ii) Deshbandhu
(iii) Mahamana
(iv) Man of Peace

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri is remembered as the 'Man of Peace' (he died at Tashkent after signing the peace declaration), Chittaranjan Das was titled 'Deshbandhu' for his sacrifices in Bengal, Madan Mohan Malaviya was called 'Mahamana' by Gandhi and founded Banaras Hindu University, and Bal Gangadhar Tilak was hailed as 'Lokmanya'. The option pairing Shastri with 'Deshbandhu' is wrong because that title belongs exclusively to C. R. Das. The option pairing Malaviya with 'Deshbandhu' and Das with 'Mahamana' simply interchanges two correct titles. The option pairing Shastri with 'Lokmanya' and Tilak with 'Man of Peace' reverses the two most famous attributions.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The population of a town rose by 10% during the first year and by a further 20% during the second year. If its present population is 13,200, what was the population two years ago?
questions.explanation: Let the earlier population be P. Then P x 1.10 x 1.20 = 13,200, i.e. P x 1.32 = 13,200, so P = 10,000. Checking forward: 10,000 becomes 11,000 after the first year and 13,200 after the second. '11,000' is wrong because that is the population after ONE year, not two years ago. '10,500' is wrong because it comes from reducing 13,200 by a flat 20% and then adjusting roughly, instead of dividing by the combined factor. '12,000' is wrong because it results from dividing 13,200 by 1.10 only, ignoring the second year's growth.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the idioms in Column I with their meanings in Column II:

Column I:
(a) To let the cat out of the bag
(b) To turn a deaf ear
(c) To pay through the nose
(d) To be in the same boat

Column II:
(i) To refuse to listen to a request
(ii) To be in an equally difficult situation
(iii) To reveal a secret unintentionally
(iv) To pay an excessively high price

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to disclose a secret accidentally; 'turn a deaf ear' means to ignore or refuse to listen; 'pay through the nose' means to pay far too much; 'in the same boat' means to share the same difficulty. The option linking the cat idiom to 'refuse to listen' is wrong because it swaps two unrelated idioms. The option linking 'turn a deaf ear' to 'pay an excessively high price' is wrong because the deaf-ear idiom concerns listening, never money. The option linking the cat idiom to 'equally difficult situation' is wrong because that meaning belongs to 'in the same boat', which is about shared circumstances, not disclosure.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Match the MS Word keyboard shortcuts in Column I with their effects in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Ctrl + E
(b) Ctrl + J
(c) Ctrl + L
(d) Ctrl + R

Column II:
(i) Justify the paragraph
(ii) Align the text to the right
(iii) Centre the paragraph
(iv) Align the text to the left

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: In MS Word, Ctrl+E centres a paragraph, Ctrl+J justifies it, Ctrl+L aligns it left and Ctrl+R aligns it right. The option pairing Ctrl+E with 'justify' is wrong because justification is Ctrl+J, the letter J being the mnemonic. The option pairing Ctrl+E with 'align left' is wrong because Ctrl+L is the left-align shortcut. The option pairing Ctrl+J with 'align left' and Ctrl+L with 'justify' is wrong because it interchanges the two shortcuts whose mnemonic letters are J for justify and L for left.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations Organization:

(i) The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.
(ii) The Security Council has 15 members, of which five are permanent.
(iii) The International Court of Justice has its seat at Geneva.
(iv) The Trusteeship Council is one of the six principal organs of the UN.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Charter entered into force on 24 October 1945, now observed as UN Day. Statement (ii) is correct — the Council has 5 permanent members with veto power and 10 elected non-permanent members. Statement (iv) is correct — the six principal organs are the General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ and Secretariat. Statement (iii) is FALSE because the ICJ sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands; Geneva hosts UN offices such as the Human Rights Council and WHO. Hence every option that includes (iii) must be rejected, which rules out the other three choices.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Find the next term in the series: 3, 8, 18, 38, 78, ?
questions.explanation: The rule is 'multiply by 2 and add 2': 3x2+2 = 8, 8x2+2 = 18, 18x2+2 = 38, 38x2+2 = 78, so 78x2+2 = 158. '148' is wrong because it comes from doubling and subtracting 8, a rule that fails on the earlier terms. '156' is wrong because it is only 78 doubled, ignoring the constant +2 present at every step. '168' is wrong because it assumes the differences 5, 10, 20, 40 continue as 90 (an incorrect doubling of the last gap plus 10); the actual gap sequence is 5, 10, 20, 40, 80.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the tourist destinations of Jammu and Kashmir in Column I with their descriptions in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Pahalgam
(b) Patnitop
(c) Gulmarg
(d) Bhaderwah

Column II:
(i) Hill station in Udhampur district on the Jammu-Srinagar highway
(ii) Base camp of the Amarnath Yatra in Anantnag district
(iii) Valley in Doda district popularly called 'Mini Kashmir'
(iv) Ski resort in Baramulla district served by a Gondola

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Pahalgam in Anantnag district is the traditional base for the Amarnath Yatra; Patnitop is the well-known hill resort of Udhampur district on NH-44; Gulmarg in Baramulla district has the Gulmarg Gondola and is India's premier ski destination; Bhaderwah in Doda district is nicknamed 'Mini Kashmir'. The option placing Patnitop in Doda is wrong because Patnitop lies in Udhampur. The option pairing Pahalgam with the Gondola ski resort is wrong because the Gondola is at Gulmarg. The option pairing Pahalgam with the Udhampur hill station is wrong because Pahalgam is in the Kashmir valley, not on the Jammu-Srinagar highway in Udhampur.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence with respect to the sequence of tenses.
options: By the time the reinforcements arrived, the mob had dispersed.
By the time the reinforcements arrived, the mob has dispersed.
By the time the reinforcements had arrived, the mob has dispersed.
By the time the reinforcements arrive, the mob had dispersed.
questions.correctAnswer: By the time the reinforcements arrived, the mob had dispersed.
questions.explanation: When two past actions are described, the earlier one takes the past perfect and the later one the simple past; the dispersal happened before the arrival, so 'had dispersed' with 'arrived' is correct. The version with 'has dispersed' is wrong because the present perfect cannot be used with a definite past time frame set by 'arrived'. The version with 'had arrived ... has dispersed' is wrong because it reverses the sequence and mixes present perfect with past perfect. The version with 'arrive ... had dispersed' is wrong because a present-tense main clause cannot govern a past perfect in a completed past narrative.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Ranji Trophy, India's premier first-class domestic cricket championship, was first held in which season?
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy was instituted in 1934 in memory of Ranjitsinhji and the first tournament was played in the 1934-35 season, won by Bombay. '1928-29' is wrong because that year marks the founding of the Board of Control for Cricket in India's predecessor arrangements and India's ICC membership, not the Ranji Trophy. '1946-47' is wrong because by then the tournament had already run for over a decade. '1951-52' is wrong because that season is remembered for India's first-ever Test victory, against England at Madras, and has no connection with the inauguration of the Ranji Trophy.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
In a certain code language every letter of a word is replaced by the letter immediately following it in the English alphabet. Match the words in Column I with their codes in Column II:

Column I:
(a) BAT
(b) CAP
(c) DOG
(d) FAN

Column II:
(i) EPH
(ii) GBO
(iii) CBU
(iv) DBQ

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Applying +1 to each letter: BAT becomes CBU, CAP becomes DBQ, DOG becomes EPH and FAN becomes GBO. The option pairing BAT with DBQ is wrong because DBQ decodes back to CAP, not BAT. The option pairing BAT with EPH is wrong because EPH decodes to DOG. The option pairing CAP with EPH and DOG with DBQ is wrong because it interchanges the codes of CAP and DOG; letter-by-letter substitution shows C->D, A->B, P->Q for CAP and D->E, O->P, G->H for DOG.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about operating systems:

(i) An operating system acts as an interface between the user and the computer hardware.
(ii) Linux is an example of a single-user, single-tasking operating system.
(iii) Memory management and process scheduling are functions of an operating system.
(iv) MS-DOS provides a command-line interface.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct because the OS mediates every user request to the hardware. Statement (iii) is correct because memory management, process scheduling, file management and device control are its core functions. Statement (iv) is correct because MS-DOS is operated by typed commands at a prompt. Statement (ii) is FALSE — Linux is a multi-user, multitasking operating system; MS-DOS is the classic single-user, single-tasking example. Therefore each of the other three options, all of which include (ii), must be rejected.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the use of pronouns:

(i) In 'Each of the constables submitted their report', the pronoun agreement is faulty in formal grammar.
(ii) 'Who' is used as the object of a verb and 'whom' as the subject.
(iii) In 'The trophy which the team won is on display', 'which' is a relative pronoun.
(iv) In 'The officer spoke to myself', 'myself' is correctly used.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct because 'each' is singular and formally requires 'his or her report', not 'their report'. Statement (iii) is correct because 'which' introduces the adjective clause modifying 'trophy' and is therefore a relative pronoun. Statement (ii) is FALSE because the roles are reversed: 'who' is the subject form and 'whom' the object form. Statement (iv) is FALSE because a reflexive pronoun needs an antecedent in the same clause; the correct form is 'spoke to me'. Hence options containing (ii) or (iv) are all incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Fundamental Duties were not part of the Constitution of India as originally adopted.
Reason (R): They were inserted as Part IV-A by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct: the Constitution adopted in 1949 contained no chapter on Fundamental Duties. (R) is correct: ten duties were added as Article 51-A in a new Part IV-A by the 42nd Amendment of 1976, following the Swaran Singh Committee's report, and an eleventh was added in 2002 by the 86th Amendment. (R) directly explains (A) because the very fact that the duties had to be inserted by a later amendment is the reason they were absent originally. The second option is wrong because the explanatory link is present. The third option is wrong because (R) is factually accurate. The fourth is wrong because (A) is accurate.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the number zero:

(i) Zero is neither a positive nor a negative number.
(ii) Zero is an even number.
(iii) Division of any non-zero number by zero gives zero.
(iv) Zero is the additive identity for the set of integers.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — zero is the neutral point on the number line. Statement (ii) is correct because zero is exactly divisible by 2 (0 = 2 x 0). Statement (iv) is correct because a + 0 = a for every integer a, which is the definition of the additive identity. Statement (iii) is FALSE because division by zero is undefined, not zero; it is 0 divided by a non-zero number that equals zero. Every other option includes (iii) and is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indira Sagar Dam, one of India's largest multipurpose projects by reservoir capacity, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Indira Sagar Project is located at Narmadanagar in Khandwa district, Madhya Pradesh, on the Narmada, and is part of the Narmada Valley Development scheme along with Sardar Sarovar and Omkareshwar. 'Tapi' is wrong because the Tapi's major project is the Ukai Dam in Gujarat. 'Mahanadi' is wrong because the Mahanadi carries the Hirakud Dam in Odisha, India's longest earthen dam. 'Godavari' is wrong because the Godavari's principal barrages are Sriram Sagar and the Dowleswaram (Sir Arthur Cotton) barrage, neither of which is called Indira Sagar.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to 'ABATE'.
questions.explanation: 'Abate' means to lessen in intensity or amount, as in 'the storm abated', so 'diminish' is the closest synonym. 'Aggravate' is wrong because it means to make worse or more intense, the exact opposite of abating. 'Postpone' is wrong because it concerns delaying an event in time, whereas abatement concerns reduction in degree, not deferment. 'Persevere' is wrong because it means to continue steadfastly despite difficulty, which describes persistence rather than any decrease in force or quantity.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A dealer sells an article at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for ₹90 more, he would have made a gain of 8%. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation: Let the cost price be C. Then 0.90C + 90 = 1.08C, so 90 = 0.18C and C = ₹500. Check: selling at ₹450 is a 10% loss and at ₹540 an 8% gain, a gap of exactly ₹90. '₹450' is wrong because ₹450 is the actual SELLING price at a 10% loss, not the cost price. '₹550' is wrong because it comes from dividing 90 by 0.16, i.e. adding the percentages incorrectly as 10 + 6. '₹600' is wrong because it corresponds to dividing 90 by 0.15, which would require a gain of 5% instead of 8%.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the means of transport in Jammu and Kashmir:

(i) National Highway 44 is the main road link between Jammu and Srinagar.
(ii) The Jawahar Tunnel under the Pir Panjal range was opened to traffic in 1956.
(iii) The Banihal-Qazigund road tunnel shortens the Jammu-Srinagar journey and avoids the older higher-altitude stretch.
(iv) Srinagar was linked to the rest of the Indian railway network by a broad-gauge line completed in 1990.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the old NH-1A was renumbered NH-44 and remains the arterial road link to the valley. Statement (ii) is correct — the Jawahar Tunnel, the first all-weather crossing of the Pir Panjal, was thrown open in December 1956. Statement (iii) is correct — the newer Banihal-Qazigund tunnel cuts distance and travel time and keeps traffic below the snow-prone higher stretch. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the Kashmir valley was joined to the national rail network only much later, through the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla project whose Chenab bridge section was completed in the 2020s, so every option containing (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: In MS Excel, which feature displays only the rows meeting a condition you specify and temporarily hides the remaining rows?
questions.explanation: The Filter (AutoFilter) tool adds drop-down arrows to column headings and shows only the records satisfying the chosen criteria, leaving the other rows hidden but intact. 'Sort' is wrong because sorting merely rearranges all the rows in ascending or descending order and hides nothing. 'Conditional Formatting' is wrong because it changes the appearance — colour, font or icon — of cells meeting a condition while still displaying every row. 'Freeze Panes' is wrong because it only locks selected rows or columns on screen while scrolling.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the sentence 'Neither the inspector nor the constables were present at the parade', the verb form 'were' is correct.
Reason (R): With the correlative 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the subject placed nearer to it.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because the nearer subject 'constables' is plural, so the plural verb 'were' is required. (R) is correct because the proximity rule governs 'either ... or', 'neither ... nor' and 'not only ... but also'. (R) explains (A) precisely, since it is the proximity rule that forces the plural form here. The second option is wrong because the link between rule and sentence is direct. The third option is wrong because the proximity rule is a genuine rule of concord. The fourth option is wrong because 'were' is indeed the correct form in the given sentence.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The wheat production (in lakh tonnes) of four Indian states in a particular year was:

State P → 120
State Q → 150
State R → 90
State S → 140

The production of State R is what percentage less than the production of State Q?
questions.explanation: The shortfall is 150 - 90 = 60 lakh tonnes, and it must be expressed as a percentage of the reference value Q: (60/150) x 100 = 40%. '60%' is wrong because it mistakenly reports R as 60% OF Q rather than the percentage by which it is less. '33.3%' is wrong because it uses 30/90 or divides the difference by the wrong base. '66.7%' is wrong because it takes the difference 60 as a percentage of 90, i.e. it uses the smaller quantity R as the base instead of Q as the question demands.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Every prime number is an odd number.
Reason (R): A prime number has exactly two distinct positive factors, namely 1 and the number itself.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: (A) is FALSE because 2 is a prime number and it is even; it is the only even prime, which is exactly why 'all primes are odd' fails. (R) is TRUE because the definition of a prime is a natural number greater than 1 with exactly two distinct positive divisors. The first option is wrong because (A) is false, so no explanatory relation can hold. The second option is wrong for the same reason. The third option is wrong because it inverts the truth values — it is (A), not (R), that is defective.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A firewall helps prevent unauthorised access between a private network and the internet.
Reason (R): A firewall scans the hard disk and removes viruses already stored on the computer.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because a firewall filters incoming and outgoing traffic according to security rules and blocks unauthorised connections. (R) is FALSE because detecting and removing viruses already resident on a disk is the work of antivirus software; a firewall monitors network traffic, not stored files. The first option is wrong because (R) is untrue. The second option is wrong for the same reason, since it also requires (R) to be true. The fourth option is wrong because (A) is a correct description of a firewall's purpose.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: The Inspector asked, "Where were you on the night of 12 June?"
The Inspector asked "where were you on the night of 12 June?".
The Inspector asked, "where were you on the night of 12 June"?
The Inspector asked; "Where were you on the night of 12 June?"
questions.correctAnswer: The Inspector asked, "Where were you on the night of 12 June?"
questions.explanation: A direct quotation is introduced by a comma, begins with a capital letter, and keeps its own question mark inside the closing quotation marks. The second option is wrong on two counts: it omits the introductory comma and starts the quotation with a small letter. The third option is wrong because the quotation begins with a small letter and the question mark is placed outside the quotation marks even though the question belongs to the quoted words. The fourth option is wrong because a semicolon cannot introduce direct speech; a semicolon joins two independent clauses.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Dhyan Chand Award, instituted by the Government of India in 2002, is conferred for:
options: Outstanding performance in a single year
Promotion of sports by an organisation
questions.explanation: The Dhyan Chand Award recognises lifetime achievement and a sustained contribution to sports, including work after retirement from active competition. 'Outstanding performance in a single year' is wrong because that describes the Arjuna Award and the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, which honour recent competitive performance. 'Excellence in coaching' is wrong because coaching is recognised by the Dronacharya Award. 'Promotion of sports by an organisation' is wrong because institutional promotion is recognised by the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Read the following data and answer the question that follows.

The marks obtained by five students in a test of maximum 50 marks were:

Amit → 34
Binita → 41
Chandan → 28
Deepa → 45
Esha → 32

The average marks of the five students, expressed as a percentage of the maximum marks, is:
questions.explanation: Total = 34 + 41 + 28 + 45 + 32 = 180, so the average is 180/5 = 36 marks. As a percentage of 50 this is (36/50) x 100 = 72%. '68%' is wrong because it corresponds to an average of 34, which is Amit's individual score rather than the group mean. '70%' is wrong because it comes from rounding the total to 175 or from taking the average as 35. '74%' is wrong because it corresponds to an average of 37, which results from an addition error of +5 in the total.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are examples of the correct use of the apostrophe?

(i) The children's playground was renovated last year.
(ii) The two constables' uniforms were torn in the scuffle.
(iii) It's going to rain before the parade begins.
(iv) The dog wagged it's tail happily.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct because 'children' is an irregular plural not ending in -s, so the possessive adds apostrophe + s. (ii) is correct because 'constables' is a regular plural ending in -s, so only an apostrophe is added after the s. (iii) is correct because 'it's' is the contraction of 'it is'. (iv) is WRONG because the possessive of 'it' is 'its' with no apostrophe; 'it's' there would read 'it is tail'. Hence every option containing (iv) must be rejected.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kishanganga Hydroelectric Project, which Pakistan challenged under the Indus Waters Treaty, is built on a tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: The Kishanganga (Neelum) is a tributary of the Jhelum, and the run-of-the-river project in Bandipora district diverts its water to the Bonar Madmati nallah before it rejoins the Jhelum system, which is why Pakistan raised the diversion issue before the Court of Arbitration. 'Chenab' is wrong because the Chenab hosts Baglihar, Salal, Dulhasti and Ratle, not Kishanganga. 'Indus' is wrong because Indus-based projects in the region include Nimoo Bazgo and Chutak in Ladakh. 'Ravi' is wrong because the Ravi is an Eastern River allotted wholly to India and was never the subject of this dispute.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about SAARC and ASEAN:

(i) SAARC was established in 1985 and its Secretariat is at Kathmandu.
(ii) Afghanistan became the eighth member of SAARC in 2007.
(iii) ASEAN was established in 1967 by the Bangkok Declaration.
(iv) The ASEAN Secretariat is located at Kuala Lumpur.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — SAARC was founded by the Dhaka Declaration of 8 December 1985 and its Secretariat was set up at Kathmandu in 1987. Statement (ii) is correct — Afghanistan joined at the 14th Summit in New Delhi in 2007, taking membership to eight. Statement (iii) is correct — ASEAN was created on 8 August 1967 by the Bangkok Declaration signed by five founding states. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the ASEAN Secretariat is at Jakarta, Indonesia; Kuala Lumpur is the Malaysian capital but not the Secretariat's seat, so all options containing (iv) fail.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A man starts from his house and walks 4 km towards the north, then turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 4 km. How far is he from his house and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east, so he covers 3 km east; the next right turn makes him face south, and 4 km south exactly cancels the initial 4 km north. Only the 3 km eastward displacement remains, so he is 3 km east of his house. '3 km west' is wrong because a right turn from north leads east, not west. '5 km east' is wrong because it applies Pythagoras to 3 and 4 even though the north and south legs cancel, leaving no perpendicular component. '4 km east' is wrong because it mistakes the last southward leg of 4 km for an eastward one.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'RELUCTANT'.
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling and slow to act, so its antonym is 'eager', meaning keenly willing. 'Hesitant' is wrong because it is a synonym of reluctant, describing the same holding back. 'Anxious' is wrong because it chiefly means worried; even in its sense of 'anxious to help' it carries the colouring of unease rather than the plain willingness that opposes reluctance. 'Careless' is wrong because it is the opposite of 'careful' and concerns attention to detail, not willingness to act.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Which of the following secondary storage media uses a laser beam to read and write data?
questions.explanation: A DVD is an optical medium: a laser beam burns and reads pits and lands on the reflective layer of the disc. 'Hard disk drive' is wrong because it stores data as magnetic patterns on rotating platters read by a magnetic head. 'Solid state drive' is wrong because it stores data as electrical charge in NAND flash memory cells with no moving or optical parts. 'Magnetic tape' is wrong because it records data magnetically on a coated plastic ribbon and is used mainly for sequential backup, not optically.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The currency of Myanmar is the:
questions.explanation: Myanmar's currency is the Kyat, issued by the Central Bank of Myanmar. 'Kip' is wrong because the Kip is the currency of Laos, a neighbouring South-East Asian state often confused with Myanmar in currency lists. 'Ringgit' is wrong because the Ringgit is Malaysia's currency. 'Baht' is wrong because the Baht belongs to Thailand, which shares a long border with Myanmar but has an entirely separate monetary unit.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Which of the following numbers are exactly divisible by 11?

(i) 4,32,113
(ii) 9,08,721
(iii) 1,23,321
(iv) 5,04,571

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 11 when the alternating sum of its digits (from the right) is 0 or a multiple of 11. For 4,32,113: 3 - 1 + 1 - 2 + 3 - 4 = 0, divisible (432113 = 11 x 39283). For 9,08,721: 1 - 2 + 7 - 8 + 0 - 9 = -11, divisible (908721 = 11 x 82611). For 1,23,321: 1 - 2 + 3 - 3 + 2 - 1 = 0, divisible (123321 = 11 x 11211). For 5,04,571 the alternating sum is 1 - 7 + 5 - 4 + 0 - 5 = -10, which is not a multiple of 11, so (iv) fails and every option containing it is wrong.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: If he __________ harder, he would have qualified for the physical endurance test. Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: __________
questions.explanation: The main clause 'would have qualified' marks this as a third conditional about an unreal past, and the if-clause of a third conditional takes the past perfect, hence 'had trained'. 'has trained' is wrong because the present perfect cannot appear in the if-clause of an unreal past condition. 'would train' is wrong because 'would' belongs in the result clause, never in the if-clause of a standard conditional. 'trained' is wrong because the simple past belongs to the second conditional ('if he trained, he would qualify'), which refers to an unreal present, not a lost past opportunity.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are recognised as classical languages by the Government of India?

(i) Tamil
(ii) Sanskrit
(iii) Marathi
(iv) Urdu

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Tamil was the first language to receive classical status (2004) and Sanskrit followed (2005). Marathi was granted classical status in 2024 along with Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali, taking the list to eleven. Urdu, though one of the 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule and an official language of several states, has NOT been declared a classical language, so it does not qualify. Every option containing (iv) is therefore wrong, and the option that omits Tamil ignores the very first language to be so recognised.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A car covers a distance of 210 km in 3 hours. What speed must it maintain to cover the same distance in 2 hours 30 minutes?
questions.explanation: Required speed = distance/time = 210 / 2.5 = 84 km/h. '80 km/h' is wrong because it comes from dividing 210 by 2.625 or from rounding the time to 2 hours 38 minutes. '88 km/h' is wrong because it results from taking the time as 2 hours 23 minutes, i.e. treating '30 minutes' as 0.30 of an hour incorrectly in the reverse direction. '90 km/h' is wrong because it corresponds to 210 divided by 2.33 hours, which would be 2 hours 20 minutes rather than 2 hours 30 minutes.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are input devices?

(i) Optical Mark Reader
(ii) Plotter
(iii) Barcode scanner
(iv) Microphone

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: An Optical Mark Reader senses pencil marks on answer sheets, a barcode scanner reads printed bar patterns and a microphone converts sound into digital signals — all of these feed data INTO the computer. A plotter is an OUTPUT device: it draws large-format engineering and architectural diagrams on paper using pens or ink, so it delivers data out of the computer. Consequently every option that includes (ii) is incorrect, and the option omitting the microphone wrongly excludes a genuine audio input device.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Kashmir Valley receives a substantial share of its annual precipitation during winter and early spring.
Reason (R): The valley lies in the path of western disturbances that travel eastwards from the Mediterranean region.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct: unlike most of India, the Kashmir Valley gets heavy winter and spring precipitation, much of it as snow, which sustains the Jhelum and the spring-sown crops. (R) is correct: extra-tropical western disturbances originating over the Mediterranean and Caspian region move eastwards and are the main rain-bearing systems for the valley, while the summer monsoon is largely blocked by the Pir Panjal. (R) therefore explains (A) directly. The second option is wrong because the causal link is genuine. The third is wrong because western disturbances are a well-established fact. The fourth is wrong because (A) is accurate.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the sentence in which the homophone has been used correctly.
options: The bus remained stationery at the level crossing.
The principle of the college addressed the gathering.
The stationary shop near the gate sells notebooks.
The principal of the college addressed the gathering.
questions.correctAnswer: The principal of the college addressed the gathering.
questions.explanation: 'Principal' as a noun means the head of an institution, so 'the principal of the college' is right. The option using 'principle' is wrong because 'principle' means a fundamental rule or doctrine and can never denote a person who addresses a gathering. The option with 'stationary shop' is wrong because 'stationary' means motionless, whereas a shop selling notebooks deals in 'stationery'. The option with 'stationery' for the bus is wrong because a halted vehicle is 'stationary'; 'stationery' refers to writing materials.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: 'Amrita Bazar Patrika', one of the earliest Indian-owned English dailies, was founded by:
questions.explanation: Amrita Bazar Patrika was started in 1868 by Sisir Kumar Ghosh along with his brother Motilal Ghosh, first in Bengali and later in English, and became a strong nationalist voice. 'Surendranath Banerjee' is wrong because he founded 'The Bengalee'. 'Robert Knight' is wrong because he was a British journalist who founded 'The Statesman' and edited 'The Times of India', so the paper would not have been Indian-owned. 'Girish Chandra Ghosh' is wrong because he was associated with 'The Bengalee' in its early phase and with Bengali theatre, not with the founding of Amrita Bazar Patrika.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements and the conclusions drawn from them:

(i) All members of the SDRF team are trained in rope rescue.
(ii) Some persons trained in rope rescue are certified divers.
(iii) Conclusion: Some members of the SDRF team are certified divers.
(iv) Conclusion: All certified divers are trained in rope rescue.

Which of the conclusions (iii) and (iv) is/are logically invalid?
questions.explanation: Conclusion (iii) is invalid because the divers who are rope-trained may all lie outside the SDRF team; a 'some' overlap in the wider class guarantees nothing about the subset. Conclusion (iv) is invalid because the premise runs from rope-trained persons to divers, not the reverse; a diver who has never done rope training is entirely consistent with both premises. Hence '(iii) only' and '(iv) only' are wrong because each wrongly certifies the other conclusion as valid, and 'Neither (iii) nor (iv)' is wrong because it accepts two inferences that both commit the illicit-conversion error.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the analogy pairs in Column I with the relationship each expresses in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Carpenter : Chisel
(b) Kitten : Cat
(c) Miser : Generous
(d) Petal : Flower

Column II:
(i) Part and whole
(ii) Worker and tool
(iii) Young one and adult
(iv) Antonyms

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: A chisel is the tool a carpenter works with (worker-tool); a kitten is the young of a cat (young-adult); miser and generous are opposed in sense (antonyms); a petal is a component of a flower (part-whole). The option pairing 'Kitten : Cat' with part and whole is wrong because a kitten is not a portion of a cat but its immature form. The option pairing 'Carpenter : Chisel' with part and whole is wrong because a chisel is not a component of a carpenter. The option pairing 'Carpenter : Chisel' with antonyms and 'Miser : Generous' with worker and tool simply exchanges two unrelated relationships.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: In an e-mail message, the addresses typed into the 'BCC' field are:
options: Visible only after the mail has been forwarded
Visible to every other recipient of the mail
Visible only to the recipients in the CC field
Hidden from every other recipient of the mail
questions.correctAnswer: Hidden from every other recipient of the mail
questions.explanation: BCC stands for Blind Carbon Copy: each BCC recipient receives the message, but no recipient — in the To, CC or BCC field — can see the BCC list. 'Visible to every other recipient' is wrong because that describes the CC field, whose addresses are openly displayed. 'Visible only to the recipients in the CC field' is wrong because CC recipients see only To and CC addresses, never BCC ones. 'Visible only after the mail has been forwarded' is wrong because forwarding carries over the visible header fields, not the concealed BCC list.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ice floats on the surface of water.
Reason (R): Water attains its maximum density at 4 degrees Celsius.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — ice floats. (R) is also correct — water is densest at about 4 degrees Celsius, the basis of its anomalous expansion. However (R) does not explain (A): ice floats because on freezing water expands into an open hexagonal lattice whose density (about 0.92 g/cc) is LESS than that of liquid water at 0 degrees Celsius. The first option is wrong because the maximum-density fact concerns liquid water between 0 and 4 degrees, not the solid state. The third and fourth options are wrong because both statements are factually true.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The average age of the 11 players of a cricket team is 25 years. When the coach's age is included, the average of the 12 persons becomes 26 years. What is the coach's age?
questions.explanation: Total age of 11 players = 11 x 25 = 275 years; total of 12 persons = 12 x 26 = 312 years; hence the coach's age = 312 - 275 = 37 years. '36 years' is wrong because it adds only the new average to the old total difference incorrectly (25 + 11 = 36), a common shortcut error. '38 years' is wrong because it uses 12 x 26 with a player total of 274, i.e. an arithmetic slip. '35 years' is wrong because it comes from assuming the coach's age simply exceeds the old average by 10, which has no basis in the data.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Mughal garden Nishat Bagh, laid out on the eastern bank of the Dal lake, was built by:
questions.explanation: Nishat Bagh, the 'garden of delight', was laid out in 1633 by Asaf Khan, the elder brother of Empress Nur Jahan, and is the largest of the Mughal terraced gardens of Srinagar. 'Jahangir' is wrong because the emperor built Shalimar Bagh for Nur Jahan. 'Shah Jahan' is wrong because his Kashmir associations are with the Chashma Shahi spring garden and the Pari Mahal patronage of his son Dara Shikoh. 'Zafar Khan' is wrong because he was a Mughal governor of Kashmir remembered for the Achabal garden's later development, not for Nishat.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The department will look ______ the allegations carefully before submitting its final report.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means to investigate or examine, which is exactly what a department does with allegations. 'after' is wrong because 'look after' means to take care of a person or thing, a sense that cannot apply to allegations. 'over' is wrong because 'look over' means to inspect something quickly or casually, which contradicts the adverb 'carefully' and the seriousness of an inquiry. 'for' is wrong because 'look for' means to search for something missing, whereas the allegations are already before the department.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the books in Column I with their authors in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Train to Pakistan
(b) The Guide
(c) Gitanjali
(d) Anandamath

Column II:
(i) R. K. Narayan
(ii) Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
(iii) Khushwant Singh
(iv) Rabindranath Tagore

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Train to Pakistan' (1956) is Khushwant Singh's Partition novel; 'The Guide' is R. K. Narayan's Sahitya Akademi-winning novel set in Malgudi; 'Gitanjali' won Rabindranath Tagore the Nobel Prize in 1913; 'Anandamath' by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay contains 'Vande Mataram'. The option swapping the first two authors is wrong because Narayan never wrote on Partition. The option pairing 'Gitanjali' with Bankim Chandra and 'Anandamath' with Tagore is wrong because it interchanges two Bengali writers of different generations. The option pairing 'Train to Pakistan' with Bankim Chandra is wrong because he died in 1894, decades before Partition.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
In a certain system of symbols, '+' means multiply, '-' means add, 'x' means subtract and '÷' means divide. Match the expressions in Column I with their values in Column II:

Column I:
(a) 8 + 3 - 4
(b) 12 ÷ 4 - 5
(c) 9 x 3 + 2
(d) 15 - 5 ÷ 5

Column II:
(i) 3
(ii) 8
(iii) 28
(iv) 16

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Substituting the symbols and then applying BODMAS: (a) 8 x 3 + 4 = 24 + 4 = 28; (b) 12 / 4 + 5 = 3 + 5 = 8; (c) 9 - 3 x 2 = 9 - 6 = 3; (d) 15 + 5 / 5 = 15 + 1 = 16. The option giving (b) the value 3 is wrong because it stops after the division and ignores the '+5'. The option giving (a) the value 16 is wrong because 16 belongs to expression (d). The option pairing (a) with 8 and (b) with 28 is wrong because it interchanges the two results and also mishandles the order of operations in (c) and (d).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Match the categories of software in Column I with their descriptions in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Firmware
(b) Freeware
(c) Shareware
(d) Open-source software

Column II:
(i) Distributed free for a trial period, after which payment is expected
(ii) Permanently written into a read-only memory chip of a device
(iii) Released with its source code available for study and modification
(iv) Available at no cost, though its source code is not released

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Firmware is software burnt into ROM or flash inside a device such as a BIOS chip; freeware is free to use but closed-source; shareware is free only for an evaluation period; open-source software publishes its source code under a permissive licence. The option pairing freeware with the trial period is wrong because a time-limited trial defines shareware, not freeware. The option pairing firmware with open source is wrong because firmware is defined by where it is stored, not by licensing. The option pairing firmware with 'no cost' and open source with 'trial period' misplaces all four descriptions.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about clauses:

(i) In 'I know that he is honest', the group 'that he is honest' is a noun clause.
(ii) In 'The man who came late was fined', the group 'who came late' is an adverb clause.
(iii) In 'He left early because he was unwell', the group 'because he was unwell' is an adverb clause of reason.
(iv) A subordinate clause can stand alone as a complete sentence.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct because 'that he is honest' works as the object of 'know', a nominal function. Statement (iii) is correct because 'because he was unwell' modifies the verb 'left' by supplying a reason. Statement (ii) is FALSE because 'who came late' qualifies the noun 'man' and is therefore an adjective (relative) clause. Statement (iv) is FALSE because a subordinate clause depends on a main clause for completeness; standing alone it is a fragment. Hence any option containing (ii) or (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about centrally sponsored schemes:

(i) The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana aims at universal access to banking facilities.
(ii) Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides health cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care.
(iii) PM-KISAN provides direct income support to landholding farmer families.
(iv) The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched in the year 2019.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — PMJDY, launched in 2014, targets universal financial inclusion through zero-balance accounts. Statement (ii) is correct — PM-JAY offers ₹5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation in secondary and tertiary care. Statement (iii) is correct — PM-KISAN transfers ₹6,000 a year in three instalments to eligible landholding farmer families. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014; 2019 was the year the rural sanitation target was declared achieved, so all options containing (iv) are wrong.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The area of a square is equal to the area of a rectangle 16 cm long and 9 cm broad. What is the perimeter of the square?
questions.explanation: Area of the rectangle = 16 x 9 = 144 sq cm, so the side of the square = square root of 144 = 12 cm and the perimeter = 4 x 12 = 48 cm. '50 cm' is wrong because it corresponds to a side of 12.5 cm, obtained by averaging 16 and 9. '44 cm' is wrong because it is the perimeter of the RECTANGLE, 2(16 + 9), not of the square. '36 cm' is wrong because it corresponds to a side of 9 cm, i.e. it wrongly takes the breadth of the rectangle as the side of the square.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The rock-cut Kailasa temple, carved downwards out of a single mass of rock, is located at:
questions.explanation: Cave 16 at Ellora in Maharashtra is the Kailasa temple, excavated from the top downwards out of one basalt outcrop under the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I, and Ellora is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 'Ajanta' is wrong because the Ajanta caves are Buddhist chaityas and viharas famous for murals, not a monolithic Hindu temple. 'Elephanta' is wrong because Elephanta near Mumbai has rock-cut caves with the Trimurti sculpture but no free-standing monolithic temple. 'Mahabalipuram' is wrong because its monoliths are the smaller Pancha Rathas of the Pallavas, not the Kailasa temple.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'to steal a march' mean?
options: To copy another person's written work
To move rapidly during a ceremonial parade
To gain an advantage secretly over a rival
To withdraw from a contest without notice
questions.correctAnswer: To gain an advantage secretly over a rival
questions.explanation: 'To steal a march (on someone)' comes from military usage where an army moved quietly to gain ground, and it now means to secure an advantage by acting before or without the knowledge of a rival. 'To move rapidly during a ceremonial parade' is wrong because it takes 'march' in its literal drill sense and ignores the idiomatic meaning. 'To copy another person's written work' is wrong because that is plagiarism, expressed by idioms such as 'lift material'. 'To withdraw from a contest without notice' is wrong because withdrawal is the opposite of gaining ground on a competitor.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the letter series B, D, G, K, P, the next letter is V.
Reason (R): The gap between consecutive letters increases by one each time, being +2, +3, +4, +5 and then +6.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct: using positions B=2, D=4, G=7, K=11, P=16, adding 6 gives 22, which is V. (R) is correct because the gaps are exactly 2, 3, 4, 5 and then 6. (R) is the reason (A) holds, since the widening gap is what fixes the next letter. The second option is wrong because the rule stated is precisely the rule that generates the answer. The third option is wrong because the gap pattern is genuine and verifiable. The fourth option is wrong because V is indeed the correct next letter.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are freshwater lakes of the Kashmir valley?

(i) Wular
(ii) Manasbal
(iii) Sambhar
(iv) Dal

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Wular in Bandipora is one of Asia's largest freshwater lakes and acts as a flood absorber for the Jhelum; Manasbal near Safapora is the deepest lake of the valley and a noted lotus habitat; Dal in Srinagar is a freshwater urban lake famous for houseboats and floating gardens. Sambhar is NOT in Kashmir at all — it is India's largest inland SALT lake, situated in Rajasthan, so every option containing (iii) is wrong, and the option omitting Dal excludes the valley's best-known freshwater lake.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: A named collection of related records held together in secondary storage is called a __________.
questions.explanation: The data hierarchy runs bit → byte → field → record → file → database, so a set of related records stored under one name is a file. 'field' is wrong because a field is a single data item such as a name or roll number, the smallest meaningful unit within a record. 'record' is wrong because a record is one complete set of fields about a single entity, and many records together make a file. 'byte' is wrong because a byte is a storage unit of eight bits and represents just one character, far below the level of records.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Identify the kind of subordinate clause in the sentence: 'Wherever the police party went, the crowd followed.'
questions.explanation: 'Wherever the police party went' is introduced by the conjunction 'wherever' and modifies the verb 'followed' by telling WHERE the action happened, making it an adverb clause of place. 'Adjective clause' is wrong because the group does not qualify any noun or pronoun in the main clause. 'Noun clause' is wrong because it cannot be replaced by a noun or pronoun functioning as subject or object. 'Adverb clause of time' is wrong because 'wherever' expresses place; a time clause would begin with 'when', 'while', 'as soon as' or 'until'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: A form of government in which powers are divided between a central authority and constituent units, each supreme in its own sphere, is called a __________ government.
questions.explanation: A federal system distributes legislative and executive powers between the Union and the states through a written constitution, as India does through the Seventh Schedule. 'unitary' is wrong because in a unitary state all authority is concentrated in the centre, which may delegate powers but retains supremacy. 'confederal' is wrong because in a confederation the constituent states remain sovereign and the central body derives its limited powers from them. 'presidential' is wrong because that term describes the relation between the executive and the legislature, not the territorial division of powers.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If 40% of a number is 56, then 75% of the same number is:
questions.explanation: If 40% of the number is 56, the number is 56 x 100/40 = 140, and 75% of 140 is 105. '112' is wrong because it is 80% of 140, obtained by simply doubling 56 instead of scaling from 40% to 75%. '98' is wrong because it is 70% of 140, the result of misreading the required percentage. '120' is wrong because it assumes the number itself is 160, which would make 40% equal 64 rather than 56.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: While using a search engine, enclosing a group of words in double quotation marks makes the engine:
options: Return pages containing that exact phrase
Exclude pages containing that group of words
Search for the words only within one website
Return pages containing any one of those words
questions.correctAnswer: Return pages containing that exact phrase
questions.explanation: Double quotation marks force an exact-phrase search, so the words must appear together in the same order. 'Exclude pages containing that group of words' is wrong because exclusion is done with the minus operator, as in -advertisement. 'Search for the words only within one website' is wrong because restricting to a single domain requires the site: operator, for example site:nic.in. 'Return pages containing any one of those words' is wrong because that is the default OR-like broad behaviour that quotation marks are used to prevent.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly formed comparative or superlative structures?

(i) This route is more safer than the highway.
(ii) He is the tallest of the three constables.
(iii) She is more intelligent than her elder sister.
(iv) This is the most unique specimen in the museum.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (ii) is correct because with three or more items the superlative 'tallest of the three' is required. (iii) is correct because polysyllabic adjectives such as 'intelligent' form the comparative with 'more'. (i) is WRONG because 'more safer' is a double comparative; either 'safer' or 'more safe' may be used, never both. (iv) is WRONG because 'unique' is an absolute adjective meaning one of a kind and cannot be graded with 'most'. Therefore every option that includes (i) or (iv) must be rejected.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which gas is chiefly responsible for making dough rise when baking soda is used in baking?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate; on heating or on reacting with an acid it releases carbon dioxide, whose bubbles are trapped in the dough and make it porous and light. 'Oxygen' is wrong because no oxygen is liberated in this decomposition; oxygen supports combustion but does not leaven dough. 'Nitrogen' is wrong because nitrogen is chemically inert here and is not a product of the reaction. 'Hydrogen' is wrong because hydrogen would be produced by a metal-acid reaction, not by the decomposition of a hydrogen carbonate salt.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: In the letter-number series B2, D4, F6, H8, the next term is __________.
questions.explanation: The letters skip one place each time (B, D, F, H, J) and the numbers increase by 2 each time (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), so the next term is J10. 'I10' is wrong because I immediately follows H and breaks the alternate-letter pattern. 'J9' is wrong because it advances the number by only 1 instead of the established 2. 'K10' is wrong because K is two places beyond H and would skip J, which is the correct alternate letter after H.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The word 'news' takes a singular verb, as in 'The news is disturbing'.
Reason (R): All English nouns ending in the letter -s take a singular verb.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because 'news' is a singular uncountable noun despite its final -s, so 'The news is disturbing' is right. (R) is FALSE because many nouns ending in -s are plural and take plural verbs, such as 'trousers are', 'scissors are' and 'proceeds were'; the -s ending decides nothing by itself. The first option is wrong because a false reason cannot explain a true assertion. The second option is wrong for the same reason, since it also requires (R) to be true. The fourth option is wrong because (A) is a correct statement of usage.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: JKEDI, the agency of Jammu and Kashmir that promotes self-employment and start-ups, stands for Jammu and Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development __________.
questions.explanation: JKEDI is the Jammu and Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute, an autonomous body headquartered at Pampore that trains youth and implements self-employment schemes in the Union Territory. 'Initiative' is wrong because JKEDI is a permanent institutional body, not a programme or campaign. 'Instrument' is wrong because the expansion of the abbreviation must yield the name of an organisation, and no agency is styled an 'Instrument'. 'Incubator' is wrong because although the Institute runs business incubation activities, incubation is one of its functions and not part of its official name.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the specialised agencies of the United Nations in Column I with their headquarters and mandate in Column II:

Column I:
(a) UNESCO
(b) WHO
(c) ILO
(d) FAO

Column II:
(i) Geneva — international labour standards
(ii) Rome — food and agriculture
(iii) Paris — education, science and culture
(iv) Geneva — international public health

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: UNESCO is headquartered in Paris and works on education, science and culture; WHO is in Geneva and handles global public health; the ILO, the oldest specialised agency, is also in Geneva and sets labour standards; the FAO is in Rome and deals with food and agriculture. The option pairing WHO with labour standards and the ILO with public health is wrong because it interchanges the two Geneva-based bodies. The option placing UNESCO in Rome is wrong because Rome is the FAO's seat. The option pairing UNESCO with public health and the FAO with education reverses all four mandates.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the hands of an ordinary clock:

(i) The minute hand completes one revolution in 60 minutes.
(ii) The hour hand turns through 30 degrees in one hour.
(iii) The two hands coincide 24 times in a period of 24 hours.
(iv) At exactly 3 o'clock the angle between the two hands is 90 degrees.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct by definition of the minute hand. Statement (ii) is correct because the hour hand covers 360 degrees in 12 hours, i.e. 30 degrees per hour. Statement (iv) is correct because at 3 o'clock the hour hand is at 90 degrees and the minute hand at 0 degrees. Statement (iii) is FALSE — the hands coincide only 11 times in 12 hours and therefore 22 times in 24 hours, because the minute hand gains a full circle on the hour hand only 11 times per 12-hour cycle. Every option containing (iii) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the words in Column I with their meanings in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Candid
(b) Obstinate
(c) Lucid
(d) Prudent

Column II:
(i) Clear and easy to understand
(ii) Cautious and sensible in judgement
(iii) Frank and outspoken in expression
(iv) Stubborn and unwilling to yield

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means frank and straightforward in speech; 'obstinate' means stubbornly refusing to change; 'lucid' means clearly expressed and easily understood; 'prudent' means showing care and good sense. The option pairing 'candid' with 'clear and easy to understand' is wrong because that sense belongs to 'lucid', which describes expression, not honesty. The option pairing 'obstinate' with 'cautious and sensible' is wrong because obstinacy is a defect of inflexibility, not a virtue of judgement. The option pairing 'candid' with 'cautious' and 'prudent' with 'frank' interchanges two quite different qualities.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Data held in RAM is lost when the computer is switched off.
Reason (R): RAM is called Random Access Memory because any storage location in it can be reached directly without reading through the preceding locations.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because RAM is volatile memory. (R) is also correct because random access indeed means direct access to any address, in contrast with the sequential access of magnetic tape. But (R) does not explain (A): the loss of data is caused by volatility, since RAM cells hold data as an electric charge that needs a continuous power supply. The first option is wrong because access method and volatility are independent properties. The third and fourth options are wrong because both statements are factually accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In a particular year a country's merchandise exports were valued at ₹28 lakh crore and its merchandise imports at ₹45 lakh crore. What was its merchandise trade deficit for that year?
questions.explanation: A merchandise trade deficit is imports minus exports: 45 - 28 = ₹17 lakh crore. '₹73 lakh crore' is wrong because it ADDS the two figures, which gives total merchandise trade turnover, not the deficit. '₹16 lakh crore' is wrong because it results from a subtraction slip (45 - 29). '₹27 lakh crore' is wrong because it comes from subtracting the digits carelessly as 45 - 18; the deficit must be the exact excess of the import bill over export earnings.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is an acute angle, then the value of tan θ is:
questions.explanation: With sin θ = 3/5 the opposite side is 3 and the hypotenuse 5, so the adjacent side is the square root of (25 - 9) = 4. Hence tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 3/4. '4/3' is wrong because it is cot θ, the reciprocal obtained by interchanging the opposite and adjacent sides. '5/3' is wrong because it is cosec θ, hypotenuse over opposite. '5/4' is wrong because it is sec θ, hypotenuse over adjacent; only the ratio of the two legs gives the tangent.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: He plays ______ flute in the police band on ceremonial occasions.
questions.explanation: Names of musical instruments after the verb 'play' take the definite article — 'play the flute', 'play the guitar'. 'a' is wrong because the indefinite article would refer to one particular physical instrument rather than the skill of playing, which is not the sense here. 'an' is wrong on two counts: it is used before vowel sounds and 'flute' begins with the consonant sound /f/. 'no article' is wrong because omission of the article is the rule for games and sports ('play cricket'), not for musical instruments.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about crops in India:

(i) Rice is a kharif crop requiring high temperature and high humidity.
(ii) Wheat is a rabi crop sown in winter and harvested in spring.
(iii) Jute grows best in well-drained sandy desert soil.
(iv) Coffee cultivation in India is concentrated in the hills of Karnataka and Kerala.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — rice is sown with the south-west monsoon and needs above 25 degrees Celsius with heavy rainfall. Statement (ii) is correct — wheat is the principal rabi crop of the northern plains. Statement (iv) is correct — Karnataka, followed by Kerala and Tamil Nadu, dominates Indian coffee output. Statement (iii) is FALSE because jute requires hot, humid conditions and fertile, well-drained alluvial soil of the deltaic plains, especially West Bengal, and cannot grow in sandy desert soil. Hence every option containing (iii) fails.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the number series in Column I with the rule that generates it in Column II:

Column I:
(a) 2, 6, 12, 20, 30
(b) 1, 4, 9, 16, 25
(c) 2, 6, 18, 54
(d) 1, 8, 27, 64

Column II:
(i) Perfect cubes of successive natural numbers
(ii) Each term is three times the term before it
(iii) Products of two consecutive natural numbers
(iv) Perfect squares of successive natural numbers

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Series (a) is 1x2, 2x3, 3x4, 4x5, 5x6, i.e. products of consecutive natural numbers. Series (b) is 1², 2², 3², 4², 5². Series (c) multiplies by 3 each time (2, 6, 18, 54). Series (d) is 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³. The option pairing (a) with perfect squares is wrong because 2 and 6 are not squares. The option pairing (c) with cubes and (d) with a x3 rule is wrong because 8 is not 3 times 1 and 18 is not a cube. The option pairing (a) with the x3 rule is wrong because 6 x 3 is 18, not 12.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about MS Word:

(i) Mail Merge produces a set of personalised letters from one main document and a data source.
(ii) The Print Layout view displays the document as it will appear on the printed page.
(iii) A footer is the area that appears at the top margin of every page.
(iv) Ctrl + Shift + N applies the Normal style to the selected text.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Mail Merge combines a template with a recipient list to generate individual letters or labels. Statement (ii) is correct — Print Layout is the WYSIWYG view used for page setup. Statement (iv) is correct — Ctrl+Shift+N resets the selection to the Normal style. Statement (iii) is FALSE because the footer occupies the BOTTOM margin of each page; the top margin area is the header. Consequently every option that includes (iii) must be rejected.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Right to Information Act, 2005:

(i) It came into full force on 12 October 2005.
(ii) A public authority must ordinarily respond to an application within thirty days.
(iii) Information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be supplied within forty-eight hours.
(iv) The Act does not extend to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Act was passed in June 2005 and came into full operation on 12 October 2005. Statement (ii) is correct — the normal time limit for a Public Information Officer to reply is thirty days. Statement (iii) is correct — where life or liberty is involved the information must be given within forty-eight hours. Statement (iv) is FALSE because after the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 the central RTI Act applies to the Union Territory and the earlier J&K RTI Act, 2009 stands repealed, so all options containing (iv) are wrong.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: The commandant insisted __________ inspecting every barrack himself before the parade. Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: __________
questions.explanation: 'Insist' is followed by 'on' (or 'upon') and then a gerund, giving 'insisted on inspecting'. 'to' is wrong because 'insist' is never followed by an infinitive; the pattern 'insist to inspect' does not exist in standard English. 'for' is wrong because 'for' follows verbs of request or wish such as 'ask for' and 'press for'. 'at' is wrong because 'at' after verbs indicates a target or point, as in 'aim at' or 'look at', and cannot introduce the thing demanded after 'insist'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first woman to become the Chief Justice of a High Court in India?
questions.explanation: Leila Seth became Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court in 1991, the first woman to head any High Court in India; she had earlier been the first woman judge of the Delhi High Court. 'M. Fathima Beevi' is wrong because her distinction is being the first woman judge of the SUPREME COURT, appointed in 1989. 'Anna Chandy' is wrong because she was the first woman High Court JUDGE, in Kerala in 1959, but never a Chief Justice. 'Ruma Pal' is wrong because she served as a judge of the Calcutta High Court and later of the Supreme Court, without heading a High Court.

questions.subject: D
questions.explanation: By BODMAS, division and multiplication are done from left to right before addition and subtraction: 36 ÷ 6 = 6, then 6 x 3 = 18; separately 4 x 2 = 8. The expression becomes 18 + 8 - 8 = 18. '10' is wrong because it evaluates 6 x 3 as part of a wrongly bracketed 36 ÷ (6 x 3) = 2, giving 2 + 8 = 10. '26' is wrong because it omits the final subtraction of 8. '14' is wrong because it performs the addition before the multiplication of 4 and 2, treating 8 - 4 as 4 and then multiplying by 2.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence with respect to the case of pronouns.
options: Between yourself and me, the report was never filed.
Between you and I, the report was never filed.
Between you and me, the report was never filed.
Between I and you, the report was never filed.
questions.correctAnswer: Between you and me, the report was never filed.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition, so the pronouns following it must be in the objective case, giving 'between you and me'. The version with 'you and I' is wrong because 'I' is the subjective form and cannot follow a preposition. The version with 'yourself and me' is wrong because a reflexive pronoun requires an antecedent in the same clause and cannot serve as the object of a preposition here. The version with 'I and you' is wrong both for using the subjective 'I' and for violating the conventional order in which the first person is placed last.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: In the web address https://www.jkpolice.gov.in/notice.pdf, the part 'gov' indicates the:
options: Name of the file being requested
Name of the host web server
Type of organisation owning the site
questions.correctAnswer: Type of organisation owning the site
questions.explanation: 'gov' is the generic top-level domain segment showing that the site belongs to a government body, just as 'com' indicates commercial and 'edu' educational organisations, while 'in' is the country code. 'Name of the host web server' is wrong because that role is played by 'www.jkpolice'. 'Protocol used for the transfer' is wrong because the protocol is 'https', which appears before the colon and slashes. 'Name of the file being requested' is wrong because the file is 'notice.pdf', the last element of the path.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A country is said to have a favourable balance of trade when the value of its imports exceeds the value of its exports.
Reason (R): The balance of trade records only visible trade in goods, whereas the balance of payments also records services and capital flows.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: (A) is FALSE because the definition is the reverse: a balance of trade is favourable (a surplus) when EXPORTS exceed imports, and unfavourable (a deficit) when imports exceed exports. (R) is TRUE because the balance of trade covers only merchandise, while the balance of payments is the wider account including invisibles and capital movements.
