The first two options are wrong because they both require (A) to be correct. The third option is wrong because it wrongly rejects (R), which is an accurate distinction between the two accounts.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are always true for any two consecutive natural numbers?

(i) Their sum is an odd number.
(ii) Their product is an even number.
(iii) Their difference is 1.
(iv) Their highest common factor is 2.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Of any two consecutive natural numbers one is odd and one is even, so their sum is always odd, making (i) true, and their product always contains the even factor, making (ii) true. Their difference is 1 by definition, so (iii) is true. Statement (iv) is FALSE because consecutive natural numbers are co-prime and their HCF is always 1, never 2 — for example the HCF of 7 and 8 is 1. Every option containing (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Karewa formations of the Kashmir valley are especially important for the cultivation of:
questions.explanation: Karewas are lacustrine plateau deposits of clay, silt and sand along the valley margins; their well-drained soil and gentle slopes suit saffron, which is grown mainly on the Karewas of Pampore in Pulwama district, and also almonds and apples. 'Sugarcane' is wrong because it needs a long hot growing season with heavy water use, unsuited to the valley's temperate climate. 'Cotton' is wrong because cotton requires high temperature and black or alluvial soils of the peninsular and northern plains. 'Groundnut' is wrong because it is an oilseed of the semi-arid tropics, grown chiefly in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the use of articles:

(i) The definite article is used before the names of oceans and rivers.
(ii) The indefinite article 'a' or 'an' is used before plural countable nouns.
(iii) No article is normally used before the name of an individual mountain peak.
(iv) The definite article is used before the names of newspapers.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — we say the Pacific Ocean, the Jhelum. Statement (iii) is correct — individual peaks take no article, as in Mount Everest and Nanga Parbat, although ranges do take one (the Pir Panjal). Statement (iv) is correct — newspaper titles take 'the', as in The Tribune. Statement (ii) is FALSE because 'a' and 'an' are used only with singular countable nouns; plurals take 'some', 'many' or no determiner. Hence every option containing (ii) must be rejected.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are institutions of local self-government strengthened by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments?

(i) Gram Panchayat
(ii) Panchayat Samiti
(iii) Municipal Corporation
(iv) Legislative Council

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 gave constitutional status to rural bodies — the Gram Panchayat at village level and the Panchayat Samiti at block level — while the 74th Amendment covered urban bodies including Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils and Nagar Panchayats. A Legislative Council is the upper house of a STATE legislature created under Article 169 and is not a body of local self-government at all, so every option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sum of the three interior angles of a triangle is 180 degrees.
Reason (R): A triangle is a closed plane figure bounded by three straight line segments.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the angle-sum property of a plane triangle is 180 degrees. (R) is correct — that is the standard definition of a triangle. But (R) merely defines the figure and does not explain the angle sum, which is proved by drawing a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side and applying the alternate-angle property of parallel lines. The first option is wrong because a definition is not a proof. The third and fourth options are wrong because both statements are individually true.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: In computer terminology, one nibble is equal to:
questions.explanation: A nibble is a group of four bits, exactly half a byte, and is convenient because one nibble maps onto a single hexadecimal digit. '8 bits' is wrong because eight bits form a byte, which stores one character. '2 bits' is wrong because no standard unit of two bits exists in the bit-nibble-byte-word hierarchy. '16 bits' is wrong because sixteen bits form a word on many older architectures, or two bytes, which is four times the size of a nibble.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence: The constable ______ on duty at the checkpoint since six o'clock this morning.
questions.explanation: 'Since six o'clock this morning' marks an action that began in the past and continues into the present, which requires the present perfect (or present perfect continuous), hence 'has been'. 'is' is wrong because the simple present cannot be used with a 'since' phrase measuring duration up to now. 'was' is wrong because the simple past would close the action in the past and clashes with 'since'. 'will be' is wrong because the future tense cannot describe a period that started at six o'clock this morning.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first person to reach the South Pole?
questions.explanation: The Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911, ahead of the British party. 'Robert Falcon Scott' is wrong because his team arrived about five weeks later, in January 1912, and perished on the return march. 'Ernest Shackleton' is wrong because his expeditions came close to the Pole but never reached it, and he is remembered for the Endurance survival epic. 'Robert Peary' is wrong because his claimed first was the NORTH Pole in 1909, at the opposite end of the earth.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about HCF and LCM:

(i) The HCF of two co-prime numbers is always 1.
(ii) The LCM of two numbers is never smaller than either of the numbers.
(iii) The product of the HCF and the LCM of two numbers equals the product of the numbers.
(iv) The LCM of two distinct prime numbers is their difference.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct by the definition of co-prime numbers. Statement (ii) is correct because the LCM is a common multiple of both numbers and so is at least as large as each. Statement (iii) is correct — HCF x LCM = product of the two numbers, a standard identity for a pair of numbers. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the LCM of two distinct primes is their PRODUCT, for example the LCM of 5 and 7 is 35, not 2. Hence every option containing (iv) is wrong.
